Hey Alex / team — happy to join the sync. Quick answers to the technical bullets so you have something to review before Fri: 

1) Auth / token rotation:
- We support bearer tokens with short TTLs and token introspection endpoints for server-to-server flows. Our SDK has an integration that calls your Vault to fetch rotated tokens; alternatively we can support mTLS for the Private deployment.

2) Chat vs Completions (when to use which):
- Use chat when you need structured turn-taking, system messages, or tool-calling. Chat responses preserve role-level metadata (user/system/assistant) that helps with tool invocation.
- Use completions for single prompt/response patterns where you control the entire prompt and want a simpler request shape.

3) Tokenization / max_tokens / stop:
- Tokenization: we publish the tokenizer mapping per model; token counting for max_tokens is applied at the model input and output level. Beware that function/tool arguments serialized into the prompt count toward the limit.
- max_tokens: this controls the max tokens in the response (output). For streaming, we allocate the output budget up front; if you set max_tokens=128 the stream will end when that budget is exhausted or when a stop sequence is seen.
- stop sequences: supported for both chat and completions. For structured output we recommend using JSON Schema validation on the assistant content and also a sentinel stop like "\n\n===END===" to avoid trailing tokens.

4) Streaming semantics:
- We stream token chunks incrementally; partial chunks can be used for optimistic UI, but we guarantee a final completion event with metadata (finish_reason: stop|length|function_call).
- For tool-calling: we support 'function_call' in chat. The runtime will emit a function_call object when the model indicates it — you can intercept the call in the stream, execute the action, and resume the conversation with the result.

5) Embeddings & reranker:
- We recommend computing candidate embeddings client-side, sending a shortlist to Redwood's reranker endpoint. You can choose to store cached embeddings in your vector DB. Our SDK includes helpers for batching embeddings and a rerank endpoint that expects precomputed candidate IDs plus dense vectors.

Sample request examples attached in rsp_schema_draft.yaml (chat + function_call example, completions example, streaming headers). Happy to walk through lines on Friday.
